html:
Michael Somare led Papua New Guinea to independence on 16 September 1975 and was its first prime minister. He held the office three times, for some seventeen years in all, and is called the father of the nation.

From the Sepik, he was a teacher and broadcaster who founded the Pangu Party in 1967. He pushed Australia to grant self-government faster than many expected, and kept together a country of hundreds of peoples that some feared would break apart.

At independence he faced a secession bid by Bougainville, a forerunner of the later Bougainville war. He sits beside Walter Lini and Peter Kenilorea among Melanesia's founding leaders.
